senses.gloss: ch. same (Targ. O. ed. Berl. a. oth. עִיב׳, without Dagesh) grain, breadstuff.
units: <cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 27:28">Targ. Gen. XXVII, 28</cite>; <cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 27:37">37</cite> (h. text <he>דגן</he>).
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Isaiah 62:8">Targ. Is. LXII, 8</cite>.
<cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 41:35">Targ. Gen. XLI, 35</cite>, sq. (h. text <cite ref="A01697"><he>אכל</he></cite>); a. fr.—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Demai 1:3:12">Y. Dem. I, 22ᵃ</cite> top <cite ref="P00492"><he>עִיבּוּרָן</he></cite> our grain.

Y. Ned. VII, 40ᶜ top דגנה מעִבּוּרָהּ (perh. to be read מַעֵבוּרָהּ) by d’ganah we understand, of its (Palestine’s) breadstuff (and not Egyptian beans), v. דְּגָנָא,—Pl. עִיבּוּרַיָּיא. [Targ. Y. Gen. XVIII, 3 ed. Amst., v. עֲבוֹרָא.]—Y. Dem. l. c. מהי ע׳ עבידין how are the crops?; Y. Taan. III, 66ᶜ top.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 3:2">Targ. Job III, 2</cite> <he>על ע׳ ליליא</he> (not <he>וליליא</he>).
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Genesis 25:24">Targ. Y. Gen. XXV, 24</cite>.—

<cite ref="Niddah 40a:28">Nidd. 40ᵃ</cite> <he>בחד ע׳ כגין וכ׳</he> two confinements of one pregnancy, as was the case with Judah and Hizkiah (who were born three months apart from one another).—Pl. <he>עִיבּוּרֵי</he>, <cite ref="P00560"><he>עִכּ׳</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Niddah 40a:28">Ib.</cite> <he>בתרי ע׳</he> two confinements of two conceptions (one being a miscarriage).

senses.gloss: intercalation, proclamation of a full month; proclamation of a leap-year.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on I Samuel 20:27">Targ. I Sam. XX, 27</cite>; <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on I Samuel 20:34">34</cite> <he>יום ע׳ ירחא תנינא</he> the second New Moon Day which is observed in consequence of the proclamation of a full month.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Esther 9:31">Targ. Esth. IX, 31</cite>; Targ. II Esth. IX, 29; a. e.—

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 1:2:11">Y. Snh. I, 18ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>ועאל … קמיה מיניה לע׳</he> (not <he>מניין</he>) R. Jacob bar A. was before him admitted to the meeting for the proclamation of a leap-year; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 2:5:5">Y. R. Hash. II, 58ᵇ</cite> top; a. fr.
